Standard: When operated, under steady state and transient conditions, IAW 7.5.2, PCPs IAW 14 CFR 35.16, resist failure caused by the presence of material, manufacturing, processing, maintenance, and service-induced defects, retaining residual strength to carry maximum limit stress, for at least twice the inspection interval defined in technical data without repair. Residual strength load conditions account for changes in vibratory characteristics during usage. Initial surface flaw sizes are those detectable at the minimum demonstrated reliability (POD/CL) of the NDI methods used during manufacture and in-service maintenance. Initial embedded defect sizes/rates are characterized and controlled by material and processing controls and complementary NDI utilized during material processing and forming. Minimum flaw size detection POD/CL for all NDI methods is 90%/90%. Material and processing controls, inclusive of the following, and PCP usage tracking plans, are established: a. Material and manufacturing operation specifications throughout the procurement and production chain. b. Allowable limits and controls for material property variation. c. Critical characteristics and defect size, locations, and orientations on product definition data. d. In-process and finished-part (production and in-service) NDI requirements and acceptance standards. Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) For each PCP, review design documentation, propeller certification documentation, sustainment technical data, and product definition data that verifies: a. Compliance with material and processing control elements of this standard. b. Tracking plans. Examples of such documentation include TOs, NDI requirement definition, drawings and models, material and processing specifications. Analysis.
  (1) Controlled crack growth (fracture mechanics) analysis is conducted for each PCP. Analyses account for repeated and sustained stresses, vibratory stress (including threshold value), and include the effects of load interactions. Stress intensity is based on the structural geometry and flaw geometry. The critical stress intensity is based on the required residual strength load level or vibratory stress threshold value, and temperature conditions that exist at the component location being analyzed. Analysis initial flaw sizes are defined by the demonstrated production and sustainment NDI capabilities, or by exceedance curves for embedded defects, established IAW this standard. Limit loads used for residual strength analysis are defined for each PCP. Demonstration.
    (1) Production NDI demonstrations are performed IAW MIL-HDBK-1823 to ensure that flaws larger than the analysis initial flaw size will not occur in finished components to the reliability level required by this standard. Test.
      (1) Lab test: Propeller critical parts are selected for verification by test. These components are either pre-flawed or contain natural flaws and are cycled to verify flaw growth characteristics, strength, failure location, and failure mode and mechanism.
      (2) Lab test: Endurance testing of the propeller-and-engine combination is conducted on a sea level test stand IAW JSSG-2009, Propeller Subsystem, Propeller and Engine Test Stand Tests, 50-Hour Test, Cyclic Tests paragraph or per the conditions and success criteria as specified in 14 CFR 35.39. Post-test teardown and NDI of hardware verifies predicted damage tolerance characteristics and ability to inspect IAW technical data. Minimum endurance test duration is 50 hours.
      (3) Ground test: Installed ground testing of the integrated propeller system/engine/air vehicle is conducted on the air vehicle being certified. Static crosswind are included in the evaluation. Post-test teardown and NDI of hardware verifies predicted damage tolerance characteristics and ability to inspect IAW technical data. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Demonstration.
    (2) In-service NDI demonstrations are performed IAW MIL-HDBK-1823 to ensure that flaws larger than the corresponding analysis flaw size will not occur in released components to the reliability level required by this standard. In-service inspection flaw size detection capability is demonstrated on parts with prior operation time. Test.
    (4) Lab test: Endurance testing of the propeller-and-engine combination is conducted on a sea level test stand IAW JSSG-2009, Propeller Subsystem, Propeller and Engine Test Stand Tests, 150-Hour Test paragraph or per the conditions and success criteria as specified in 14 CFR 35.39. Post-test teardown and NDI of hardware verifies predicted damage tolerance characteristics and ability to inspect IAW technical data. Minimum endurance test duration is 150 hours.
    (5) Flight test: Flight testing of the integrated propeller system/engine/air vehicle is conducted on the air vehicle being certified. Crosswind and maneuver conditions are included in the evaluation. Post-test teardown and NDI of hardware verifies predicted damage tolerance characteristics and ability to inspect IAW technical data.
